name: Edge and End
old_description: Since 2008, Edge and End has been proud to collaborate with organizations that share our commitment to craftsmanship, education, and community impact.
about:
Edge and End operates from Providence, Rhode Island, where it was founded in 2008 by Aaron Guttin. Guttin, a lifelong woodworker who built his first toolbox at age eight, brought nearly two decades of teaching experience and a professional background spanning general contracting, luthiery, shipwright work, cabinet making, and furniture design to the venture. The company began with a mission to blend craftsmanship with community impact.

The shop produces custom woodwork for residential and commercial clients, building every piece by hand to the customer’s specifications. Materials are locally sourced hardwoods, frequently repurposed, finished with natural, food-safe coatings. The operation emphasizes sustainable sourcing and handcrafted precision, though facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not publicly disclosed.

Clients include homeowners, businesses, and nonprofit organizations. Edge and End’s pilot partner, The Groden Network, is Rhode Island’s provider for individuals with autism and developmental disabilities; the company also works with The Met School to introduce students to trade careers. Each project is fabricated in collaboration with adults with disabilities and students, integrating workforce development into the production process.

Guttin frames the business as a vehicle for creating opportunity and connection. The company states that its distinguishing feature is the integration of vulnerable community members into the making of each piece, providing trade skills, meaningful employment, and supportive pathways—turning custom furniture into a mechanism for social impact.

name: Edgework Creative
old_description: I acknowledge that this product requires freight shipping which will be charged separately after checkout is completed.
about:
Edgework Creative operates from Columbus, Ohio, where it provides custom wood and metal fabrication. The company manufactures millwork, metalwork, furniture, and fixtures for commercial and residential clients nationwide.

The shop combines woodworking and metalworking to produce custom cabinetry, stair railings, modular table systems, seating, and architectural fixtures. Projects run from prototype through full production with a quoted lead time of 12 weeks. The team handles large-scale commercial builds as well as made-to-order residential pieces, and offers free local pickup at its Columbus facility.

Edgework serves restaurants, multi-family housing, office, hospitality, retail, and sports-entertainment venues. Named projects include the Buffalo Trace Distillery Cafe, Hanks BBQ, office furniture for Delta Gamma, the Columbus Crew Premium Club, and retail fixtures for UltraShade Tattoo. Product lines such as the HIVE modular table, STAX bar stool, Mast counter stool, and Scout chair are sold directly through the company's online store.

The company positions itself on multi-material capability, value engineering, and what it calls "beautiful execution." Client testimonials describe a design-partnership approach that works through constructibility challenges before fabrication begins.

name: Eel River Brewing Company
old_description: Brewery in Fortuna, California that describes itself as the first certified organic brewery in the United States.
about:
Eel River Brewing Company is based in Fortuna, California, in the heart of Humboldt County. The brewery's organic journey began in 1998 when a customer's request for a 'naked beer' free of harmful ingredients led to the creation of its first 100% organic ale, Amber Ale. By 1999, Eel River had become the first fully certified organic brewery in the United States, establishing itself as a pioneer in organic craft brewing.

The company produces a rotating lineup of organic ales, including India Pale Ale, California Blonde, Amber Ale, and Pilsner-style ale, along with hard seltzers. In addition to brewing, Eel River operates a pub and restaurant on-site, serving food such as smoked tri-tip, burgers, and wings, and sells branded apparel through its online shop. Its beers are distributed to retail stores across the region.

Eel River serves craft beer consumers through its taproom and retail distribution, as well as restaurant patrons seeking a dog-friendly patio and live music. The brewery's products are available in stores throughout Northern California, and its pub attracts both locals and visitors camping in the Humboldt area.

The brewery emphasizes its certified organic status, sustainable and eco-friendly practices, and a commitment to using pure ingredients without artificial additives. It positions itself as independent and locally sourced, brewing without compromise on flavor or environmental responsibility.

name: Eldur Corporation
old_description: Our Glass-to-Metal Seals provide electrical connections to components in hermetic packages even under extreme conditions.
about:
Eldur Corporation, operating as the Dietze Group, is headquartered in Bangor, Maine. The company’s founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, and no founders are named in available sources.

The company manufactures hermetic interconnect components, including glass-to-metal seals, wire-based connector pins, high-precision stamped connector parts, and lead-in-wires for lighting and sensor applications. It offers custom interconnector solutions that span from concept development through series production, though facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not specified.

Eldur serves a range of industries: automotive, aerospace and military, electronics, lighting, energy, refrigeration, medical, and sensors. In automotive, its components meet the reliability demands of increasingly complex electronic systems; in aerospace and military, they withstand extreme temperatures and harsh environments; in medical, they enable hermetic sapphire windows and autoclavable connectors.

The company states its differentiation lies in providing custom interconnector solutions from concept to series production, with all products designed in close collaboration with customers and engineered to each application’s specific needs. Its mission is summarized as “We make connections!”

name: Electric Cable Compounds Inc
old_description: Independently owned global supplier, specializing in the design, development, and manufacture of thermoplastic and thermoset compounds.
about:
Electric Cable Compounds Inc (ECC) was established in 1988 in Naugatuck, Connecticut, as a privately owned and operated company. The business began as an independent global supplier focused on the design, development, and manufacture of thermoplastic and thermoset compounds for wire and cable applications.

ECC operates a non‑carbon‑black compounding facility that specializes in elastomeric, high‑performance rubber (EPR), polyolefin, and other specialty polymer‑based compounds and masterbatches. Its capabilities include custom compounding, toll mixing, formulation design, and the production of customized masterbatches with additives such as flame retardants, antioxidants, UV stabilizers, anti‑static agents, slip agents, and process aids. The site houses automated proprietary production lines with state‑of‑the‑art process control, as well as pilot‑scale equipment — Banbury mixers, twin‑screw extruders, a pilot wire line, and pilot compounding lines — supported by an on‑site laboratory staffed by chemists and technicians who conduct analytical testing (FTIR, DSC, TGA, rheology, LOI, flammability, thermal aging, moisture content, chemical compatibility, tensile/elongation/modulus, melt flow index, specific gravity, hardness) and extrusion trials.

The company’s primary market is wire and cable insulation and jacket materials, serving domestic and international customers. It also notes expansion into new markets beyond its core wire‑and‑cable focus.

ECC emphasizes its commitment to exceptional product quality, continuous improvement, and technical expertise, which it says yields compounds with a unique combination of flexibility, electrical performance, aging stability, and processability. Every box of material undergoes comprehensive testing prior to shipment to ensure consistency and reduce customer scrap.

name: Electric Control & Supply Inc

about:
Electric Control & Supply Inc, a locally owned full-line electrical distributor, has served the Midlands from Columbia, South Carolina since 1996. Founded as a local supplier to industrial and commercial customers in the region, the company has operated continuously from its Columbia base for nearly three decades, building a reputation as a reliable source for electrical materials across the central part of the state.

The company distributes a full line of electrical materials to industrial and commercial facilities, focusing on maintenance, construction, and operational needs. Its primary business is the distribution of electrical materials to industrial and commercial facilities, and it maintains store hours Monday through Thursday from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and Friday until 2:00 p.m., with after-hours sales available by arrangement to accommodate urgent requirements.

Electric Control & Supply serves industrial and commercial customers throughout the Midlands area of South Carolina, including industrial plants, commercial buildings, and contractors that require electrical supplies for ongoing operations and projects. The company emphasizes its local ownership and long-standing community presence as key differentiators in the regional market, offering after-hours service to support customer schedules.

about:
Electric Supply and Equipment Co. (ES&E) is headquartered in Greensboro, North Carolina, with an additional location in Apex. The company operates as an electrical products distributor and solutions provider serving industrial and commercial customers across the region. No founding year or founder names are disclosed in the available sources.

The company stocks and sells a broad range of electrical and automation products from brands such as Rockwell Automation and Baldor. Its catalog spans motors, wiring connectors, safety equipment, communication and specialty I/O, fasteners, hardware, tapes, insulating products, and more. Beyond product distribution, ES&E offers value-added services including a ModCenter for modifications, Rockwell Automation training courses, modernization consulting, digital transformation and analytics support, and safety program assistance. The firm also runs an e-commerce platform for online ordering.

ES&E explicitly lists DataComm/TeleComm among its served industries. Its customer base includes manufacturing operations — evidenced by product examples such as Baldor motors for fans, pumps, conveyors, and compressors — as well as facilities seeking automation, safety, and modernization solutions. Training classes are held at both the Greensboro and Apex sites, indicating a hands-on engagement with local industrial clients.

The company promotes "The ES&E Way" as its guiding philosophy, emphasizing integrity, innovation, teamwork, and a customer-centric culture aimed at delivering the lowest total cost of ownership. It positions itself as a electrical solutions partner rather than a simple reseller.

name: Electrical Components International
old_description: ECI’s roots are in Home Appliance and since 1953, we have built a legacy of leadership in space. We are the global leader of wire harnesses and control boxes to the largest Appliance OEMs worldwide.
about:
Founded in 1953 as Burcliff Industries in St. Louis, Missouri, the company was renamed Electrical Components International (ECI) in 1998. Now headquartered in Creve Coeur, Missouri, ECI has been owned by Cerberus Capital Management since 2018 and became part of Rosebank Industries in 2025.

ECI designs, engineers, and manufactures electrical distribution systems including wire harnesses, control box assemblies, and high‑voltage solutions with proprietary cable technology. The company operates 30 manufacturing facilities across nine countries with 17,000‑plus employees, managing thousands of unique SKUs for more than 400 OEM customers. Vertical integration allows custom‑engineered components to be produced in‑house, reducing lead times and simplifying supply chains.

The company serves diversified end markets such as data centers, commercial electric vehicles, advanced driver safety, aerospace and defense, medical devices, semiconductor equipment, industrial machinery, agriculture and construction, commercial lighting, and appliance and HVAC (including residential and commercial HVAC and specialty appliances). Recent customer examples include a data center operator, a global HVAC manufacturer scaling for a U.S. government contract, and a warehouse automation and robotics firm.

ECI states its mission is to create exceptional value by reliably managing complexity at scale, emphasizing global footprint with local execution, customer partnership from design through delivery, robust quality systems, on‑time delivery, supply chain resilience, and speed to market through rapid quoting and program management.

name: Electrical Contractors Hawaii, Inc.
about:
Electrical Contractors Hawaii, Inc. (ECH) was founded in 1998 on the island of Oahu, with its headquarters in Kapolei, Hawaii. The company began as a high‑voltage electrical contractor focused on federal military projects, installing substations, communications, CATV, and overhead and underground distribution systems. It is a service‑disabled veteran‑owned small business (SDVOSB).

ECH provides full‑service electrical construction, installation, and maintenance for military, government, industrial, commercial, and residential projects. Its services cover electrical substations, switchgear, communications infrastructure, fiber optics, CATV, high‑voltage and medium‑voltage work, underground and overhead distribution, runway and highway lighting, building and historical renovations, pump stations, sewer lift stations, fitness centers, and office buildings. The firm also offers electrical design consulting, value engineering, and 24‑hour emergency service. ECH employs 50–100 electricians, linemen, groundmen, and support staff, and holds C‑10, C‑62, and C‑63 licenses in Hawaii plus a General Building and C‑13 electrical license in California and Arizona.

The company’s primary customers are U.S. military branches — Army, Navy, Air Force — and federal and state government agencies. Notable projects include electrical work at Pearl Harbor, Kaneohe Marine Corps Base, Camp Pendleton, Twenty‑Nine Palms, Hanscom AFB in Massachusetts, the Kahuku Wind Farm, Onizuka Village, Capehart/Earhart Military Housing, Ford Island, and the Red Hill Mauka project. ECH also serves commercial and industrial clients such as pump stations, sewer lift stations, airport hangars, and office buildings.

ECH emphasizes a zero‑accident safety culture, earning the Associated Builders and Contractors Platinum Safety Award eight of nine years from 2003 to 2011 and multiple Excellence in Construction Grand Awards for work on military installations. The firm highlights attention to detail, dedication to quality, and an experienced supervisory workforce as key differentiators.
